newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND PICK SQUAD OF HOPEFULS TO FACE PUMAS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND PICK SQUAD OF HOPEFULS TO FACE PUMAS.

text.p: England coach Jack Rowell admitted on Wednesday that Argentina's renowned pack could put a serious dent in his side's long-term plans for the 1999 World Cup.

With 18 players required by the British Lions in South Africa, England will embark next month on a six-match tour of Argentina which Rowell acknowledges will be a major test of their reserve strength.
"I think Argentina will provide us with a big challenge," said Rowell after revealing 29 of the 30 players who will make the trip which includes two tests.
"They are very strong scrummagers, it's a way of life for them.
"I think we're going to have a useful pack. The big question will be whether the front-row can stand the pressure."
Rowell is awaiting checks on several players' fitness before confirming the identity of the 30th man -- a winger -- but sees the tour as an excellent chance for some lesser-known names.
"It is a big opportunity for back-up players to come to the forefront and stake their claim."
He added that England hopes to identify the bulk of their World Cup squad on the evidence of the Pumas tour and a solitary test against Australia in Sydney in July.

Captain Phil de Glanville, not picked by the Lions, will be joined by seven team mates from Bath including surprise pick Martin Haag at lock. The main shock among the backs is the inclusion of Sale wing David Rees.

Backs: Jim Mallinder, Mark Mapletoft, Adedayo Adebayo, Matt Allen, Jos Baxendall, Jon Sleightholme, David Rees, Phil de Glanville (captain), Nick Greenstock, Mike Catt, Alex King, Kyran Bracken, Andy Gomarsall, A.N. Other.

Forwards: Ben Clarke, Martin Corry, Tony Diprose, Chris Sheasby, Rory Jenkins, Steve Ojomoh, Garath Archer, Martin Bayfield, John Fowler, Martin Haag, Rob Hardwick, Darren Garforth, John Mallett, Kevin Yates, Phil Greening, Richard Cockerill.
